entry.title: Right in front of us, every single day, are young eyes watching

media:group.media:title: Right in front of us, every single day, are young eyes watching
media:group.media:description:
Right in front of us, every single day, are young eyes watching. They may not seem like it all the time, but they pick up way more than we realize (and more than we give them credit for).
Establishing routines and expectations are small things I can do in my classes to help us all regulate a bit and process the world around us.
The biggest hurdle for me is honestly myself - when I am stressed or tired (and I’m all that and more this week) I tend to let routines slide, BUT THAT IS WHEN WE NEED THEM MOST! Let’s check in later this week to see how well I implement my own plans…
#highschoolteacher #teacherlife #highschoolenglishteacher #dramateacher #teachermom

media:group.media:title: “I’m here
media:group.media:description:
“I’m here. I don’t have all the answers, but I’m here with you.”
What kids need when the world is its most hectic is routine - it allows their brains to begin to process and figure out what they think about what is completely and heart-breakingly out of their control.
I’m not saying that we act like nothing is wrong. I’m saying that keeping as much routine as possible allows our nervous systems to regulate (even the tiniest amount) in order to process and think critically.
#highschoolteacher #englishteacher #dramateacher

entry.title: Nobody trains you for the everyday moments - the ones that seem like they could be forgotten, and

media:group.media:title: Nobody trains you for the everyday moments - the ones that seem like they could be forgotten, and
media:group.media:description:
Nobody trains you for the everyday moments - the ones that seem like they could be forgotten, and often are.
These are the moments, though, that matter most.
These seemingly trivial moments are what builds our stamina and resolve to be all the things we are expected to be as teachers.
Each and every day, I enter school through the same gate, put my bags down in the same place, and turn on all the lights. Then, I move on to my next room and the process continues (I teach in sooooo many different rooms, but that’s a story for another day).
Why does this matter? This routine keeps me grounded and lets students know what to expect, even first thing in the morning.
Routine isn’t trivial or boring. Routine is comfort and stability… (and don’t we all need a little comfort and stability right about now?)
#highschoolteacher #teachermom #millenialteacher

media:group.media:title: Week 1 of Teaching in Real Time - to start this term on the right foot, I am putting our focus on
media:group.media:description:
Week 1 of Teaching in Real Time - to start this term on the right foot, I am putting our focus on non-tech activities as much as possible.
Instead of typing their opinions on the Freedom of Speech into a doc, American Lit students are hand-writing their work.
Instead of searching for inspiration pictures of garments for a character costume challenge, I printed pictures and pulled costume pieces to spark creativity.
And we're just on our devices looking for audition monologues because, well, you can't win them all...
Let's check in mid-week - how are things in your room?
#teacherlife #dramateacher #elateacher #teachermom #teachwithme

media:group.media:title: POV we’re coteachers and it’s the day after winter break - I’ve got the perfect activity to get our
media:group.media:description:
POV we’re coteachers and it’s the day after winter break - I’ve got the perfect activity to get our students back in school mode and ready to learn…
Activities like this one (“My 73” - we have it as a freebie on ) are great because they get students talking to each other in a controlled and low-stakes manner.
I used it with my Drama classes today to get our classroom community warmed back up so we could start brainstorming ideas for our sketch comedy unit.
Organic community building with barely any prep (literally just copies) and 10 minutes to set the tone for the week back from break - I call that a win today 🥳
Grab “My 73” over at our website for Brave New Teaching - linked in my bio!
#highschoolteacher #englishteacher #teacherlife #highschoolenglishteacher #dramateacher
